extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy; creative writers seeking philosophical/theoretical inspiration about life, consciousness, and process
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted principles from Bergson's Creative Evolution that can inform how to depict life, consciousness, and creative action in literary work — emphasizing movement, process, indeterminacy, and the interplay of individuating and associating forces. Useful for writers seeking conceptual rubrics for portraying dynamism rather than static 'things'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer actions over static things
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no things, there are only actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent becoming rather than static states: depict processes, flows, and acts rather than treating objects and persons as fixed 'things'. Bergson argues that the intellect naturally presents things and states, but the reality (and creative truth) is change and action; therefore literary representation should recover flux by privileging verbs, movement, and processual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict creation as immanent action not an external 'thing' creating
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation...is not a mystery; we experience it in ourselves when we act freely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid portraying creation as the intervention of an external, preformed entity. Instead, show creation as ongoing, embodied activity — characters, artworks, and worlds emerge through acts and choices rather than being presented as pre-existing objects imposed on matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore movement as the primary reality
rubrics_metrics.description: To movement, then, everything will be restored, and into movement everything will be resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure narrative and imagery so that motion and transformation are central: scenes should emphasize trajectories, transitions, and continuous processes. Use sequence and temporal flow to make the reader experience emergence and change rather than frozen snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show unity and multiplicity as interpenetrating (avoid purely spatialized individuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity and multiplicity are only views of my personality taken by an understanding that directs its categories at me; I enter neither into one nor into the other...the vital impetus is neither pure unity nor pure multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray selves, communities, and phenomena as overlapping, interpenetrating tendencies rather than as neatly bounded, separate entities. Use techniques (internal monologue, montage, associative jumps) that reveal the manifold aspects of a single life or the singularity within a multiplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance individuation and association
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the whole realm of life, a balancing between individuation and association...The evolution of life in the double direction of individuality and association has therefore nothing accidental about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make social form and individual identity dynamic and reciprocal: show how characters individuate and then re-associate (families, societies, colonies) and how small changes (a thread kept or cut) can flip the balance. Use plot events to explore shifts between social cohesion and personal differentiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accumulation and sudden discharge as structural principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Two things only are necessary: (1) a gradual accumulation of energy; (2) an elastic canalization of this energy in variable and indeterminable directions, at the end of which are free acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft scenes/plots that build stored potential (tension, energy, motive) and then release it in decisive acts. The mechanic of 'store then explode' can be a metaphor for pacing, character motivation, and climax: slow accrual of degrees of freedom followed by unpredictable, creative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the nervous/psychical as a growing repertoire of selectable mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The will of an animal is the more effective...the greater the number of the mechanisms it can choose from...the more developed its brain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characterizing agency, show the range of possible responses (habits, learned mechanisms, improvisations) as a locus of freedom. Emphasize how increased repertoire yields more nuanced, inventive behavior; dramatize choice by making alternatives visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray human consciousness as open-ended invention
rubrics_metrics.description: In man...the number of mechanisms it can set up...is unlimited...from the limited to the unlimited there is all the distance between the closed and the open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish human characters by their capacity for novelty, language, and creating new habits. Use language and symbolic activity in your work as the means by which consciousness extends beyond mechanistic constraints — show invention, unpredictability, and freedom of thought and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let form (verses/lines/parts) embody a unifying inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A poetic sentiment, which bursts into distinct verses, lines and words, may be said to have already contained this multiplicity of individuated elements...through the words, lines and verses runs the simple inspiration which is the whole poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using fragmentary or divided forms (poems, episodic narratives), ensure an underlying, unifying impulse or 'inspiration' runs through them. The apparent multiplicity should reveal a single living current; avoid letting fragmentation become mere disjunction without an immanent cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict life as an effort to retard material decline (creative resistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incapable of stopping the course of material changes...it succeeds in retarding it...life is entirely dependent on the chlorophyllian function...it is like an effort to raise the weight which falls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphors and narrative situations that register life/creation as resistance to entropy: accumulation, repair, preservation, and inventive uses of resources can dramatize creative will. Emphasize temporality and precariousness to heighten stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid static, mechanistic explanations of organization — prefer immanent processual causation
rubrics_metrics.description: We represent statically ready-made material particles juxtaposed...In reality, life is a movement, materiality is the inverse movement, and each of these two movements is simple...There results between them a modus vivendi, which is organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of attributing order to external designers or fixed blueprints, portray organization as emerging from interacting processes. Show how opposing currents (creative impulse vs. material necessity) generate form; dramatize the interaction rather than positing an outside 'author' of order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the image of reservoirs and jets to stage emergence and branching of worlds/ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: From an immense reservoir of life, jets must be gushing out unceasingly, of which each, falling back, is a world...the evolution of living species within this world represents what subsists of the primitive direction of the original jet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a compositional device, imagine an originating impulse (reservoir) producing offshoots (jets, worlds, stories). Each offshoot can embody a partial preservation of the original creative direction and can in turn generate its own unpredictable developments. This image helps structure generative motifs, branching plots, and thematic echoes.
